headline: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said he doubts that political spending will make people feel better about AI.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a named chief executive criticising his own industry's election spending on the record; read through a relay of the Politico interview.
importance_line: OpenAI's chief executive doubts political money will repair AI's public image, which bears on midterm voters and candidates and on the companies and groups that fund campaigns, but it is one executive's view, not a policy change.
summary: Politico reports, in an exclusive interview launching its Decoded series and as relayed by Townhall, that OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said "something's clearly not working" with the AI money flooding the midterm elections. He said he does not think political spending will make people feel better about AI, and that "a lot of people in the industry are being quite tone deaf" to real concerns; we reported another part of this interview on 5 Oct, when he said the world should accept "some bad things happening".
notes: Politico's own page returned 403 and no other outlet carries the story; text read through Townhall (5 Oct), whose opening paragraphs reproduce Politico's account of the Bordelon interview. Townhall's later commentary was not used. Same interview as 5 Oct edition item 96 (Altman: 'some bad things happening') but a different part (political spending), so not a repeat. Original not seen, hence REPORTED.
